rejection_summary.title: Lost Highway
rejection_summary.reason: Qualitative rejection: BFI's Sight and Sound analysis describes a circular, unresolved puzzle whose parallel narratives never join; Roger Ebert's full-film review finds isolated incidents without a coherent resolution, and Screen Slate notes persistent unanswered questions. Although identity instability and mysterious surveillance create suspense, the available whole-runtime evidence does not justify known integer measurements for all 30 Thriller DNA dimensions or the required meaningful-revelation cadence. Public evidence: https://www.bfi.org.uk/sight-and-sound/features/voodoo-road-marina-warner-david-lynchs-lost-highway ; https://www.rogerebert.com/reviews/lost-highway-1997 ; https://www.screenslate.com/articles/lost-highway

rejection_summary.title: Mulholland Drive
rejection_summary.reason: Qualitative rejection, not a negative assessment of film quality: BFI's Sight and Sound analysis emphasizes dream logic and a major late structural recontextualization, while Roger Ebert's whole-film review describes deliberately unresolved dream sequences and no conventional explanation; Rotten Tomatoes identifies the amnesia investigation and unconventional structure. A large late turn does not establish frequent progressive revelations throughout the runtime, and the consulted evidence is insufficient for reliable measurements of every required Thriller DNA dimension. Public evidence: https://www.bfi.org.uk/sight-and-sound/features/lethally-perfumed-neo-noir-david-lynchs-mulholland-dr ; https://www.rogerebert.com/reviews/mulholland-drive-2001 ; https://www.rottentomatoes.com/m/mulholland_dr
